questions.q: What does "serverless" mean in the context of a Glue ETL job?
options: AWS provisions and tears down the Spark cluster for you; you never manage EC2 instances or a YARN queue
The job runs without any compute at all
Glue jobs don't use Spark, only a proprietary AWS engine
You must manually launch and terminate the EC2 cluster yourself
questions.explain: Glue jobs are real Spark applications, but AWS manages the underlying cluster lifecycle — you submit a script and never touch the infrastructure.

questions.q: What is a DPU in AWS Glue?
options: A Data Processing Unit — a fixed bundle of vCPU and memory that Glue bills by the hour of usage
A type of S3 storage class
A Data Catalog table partition
A deprecated unit no longer used for billing
questions.explain: DPUs are Glue's unit of compute capacity, and billing is based on DPU-hours actually consumed while a job runs.

questions.q: Which statement correctly separates what a Glue crawler does from what a Glue job does?
options: A crawler scans data and writes schema to the Data Catalog; a job is the Spark code that actually transforms and writes data
A crawler transforms data; a job only reads metadata
They are the same component with two different names
A crawler runs Scala; a job runs Python
questions.explain: Crawlers only write metadata into the Data Catalog — they never move or transform the underlying data. That's the job's role.

questions.q: Why does the Glue Data Catalog being Hive Metastore-compatible matter?
options: It lets Athena, Redshift Spectrum, and EMR all read the same catalog entries instead of each needing a separate metadata store
It means Glue can only be used with Hadoop, not S3
It has no practical effect — it's just a marketing term
It restricts the Catalog to only storing Parquet file metadata
questions.explain: Hive Metastore compatibility is what lets multiple AWS query and processing engines share one table definition without duplicating metadata.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what does a Glue job typically rely on to know what to read?
options: Schema already registered in the Data Catalog, usually by a crawler
A manually typed CSV header pasted into the job script
Nothing — jobs always infer schema from scratch on every run
An EC2 instance's local file system
questions.explain: Jobs usually read table definitions a crawler already wrote to the Data Catalog rather than discovering schema themselves.
